 Barcelona's Raphinha doubles the home side’s lead. Photograph: Albert Gea/Reuters View image in fullscreen Barcelona's Raphinha doubles the home side’s lead. Photograph: Albert Gea/Reuters Luke McLaughlin Tue 3 Nov 2026 16.27 EST First published on Tue 3 Nov 2026 13.30 EST Share Key events 2m ago Goal! 64 min: Barcelona 3-0 Aston Villa (Raphinha) 
 14m ago Goal: 52 min: Barcelona 2-0 Aston Villa (Raphinha) 
 21m ago Second half kick off

 1h ago Goal: 7 min: Barcelona 1-0 Aston Villa (Lamine Yamal) 
 1h ago First half kick-off 
 2h ago Teams 
 3h ago Preamble 
 47s ago 16.27 EST Cancelo has McGinn on toast down the Barcelona left, ghosts towards the box, and delivers an absolutely fantastic pass, with the outside of his boot, that is met unerringly by Raphinha’s run into the six-yard box. The Brazilian hammers a shot into the corner. That’s class, and that’s 3-0. What a delivery by the former Manchester City man.
 Share Updated at  16.27 EST 2m ago 16.26 EST Goal! 64 min: Barcelona 3-0 Aston Villa (Raphinha)
 What a goal that is, by the way.
 Share 3m ago 16.25 EST 63 min: Barcelona attack again. Lamine Yamal tries a flamboyant backheel, looking for Raphinha. It nearly comes off, too.
 It appears that Hansi Flick is readying some changes …
 Share Updated at  16.25 EST 4m ago 16.23 EST 62 min: Triple change for Villa. Mbaye, Barkley, Goretzka on. Buendía, Manzambi, Gomes go off.
 Gerrard says it’s a good move by Emery because Barcelona make you work so hard off the ball.
 Share Updated at  16.24 EST 5m ago 16.22 EST 60 min: “Raphinha IS that good!” emails Mary. “Of course he is!
 “From a Leeds United supporter. We love that man.”
 As much as this man?
 View image in fullscreen Marcelo Bielsa. Photograph: Eddie Keogh/Reuters Share 8m ago 16.20 EST 58 min: Now Buendía wants a penalty for a foul by Fariñas … or at least a free-kick for a clumsy challenge on the edge with the Argentinian rushing towards goal. There is a VAR check, but anyway, it seems no luck for Villa.
 Share Updated at  16.20 EST 9m ago 16.19 EST 57 min: McGinn plays an incisive, defence-splitting pass for Jackson, on the edge of the box, and the Villa man surely needs to let the ball roll beyond him and have a shot? Bizarrely, he chooses instead to cut back, into the clutches of the covering defenders. That was a really weird bit of play by Jackson.
 Share 11m ago 16.16 EST That was Raphinha’ s 18th goal of the season. We knew he was good, but that good? Hats off to him.
 Share Updated at  16.17 EST 12m ago 16.15 EST A ball is pinged to Raphinha’s feet on the edge, the ball coming straight back into the danger zone for Villa after they have a chance to relieve the pressure. The former Leeds forward takes a couple of crisp touches, and unceremoniously clips a deflected shot low into the corner. Not much Suzuki could do about that one.
 View image in fullscreen Raphinha doubles Barcelona’s lead courtesy of a deflection. Photograph: Albert Gea/Reuters View image in fullscreen Raphinha celebrates. Photograph: Alejandro García/EPA Share Updated at  16.24 EST 14m ago 16.14 EST Goal: 52 min: Barcelona 2-0 Aston Villa (Raphinha)
 Is that overs g’dovers? You’d have to think so.
 Share 14m ago 16.13 EST 52 min: Gordon makes progress down the left flank for Barcelona . He gets to the byline but Villa deal with it. If Lamine Yamal doesn’t get you …
 Share 16m ago 16.12 EST 50 min: McGinn clatters Cancelo out near the touchline. Cancelo roars in pain, or maybe just annoyance, or maybe a bit of both.
 “Clatters’ is probably a bit much, but Cancelo went down like he’d been clattered.
 Share Updated at  16.12 EST 17m ago 16.11 EST 49 min: There is no roof at the Camp Nou due to the ongoing renovation work, I understand. Rain ponchos aplenty are visible in the crowd.
 Share Updated at  16.11 EST 19m ago 16.08 EST 46 min: Immediate danger for Villa. Lamine Yamal released to the byline on the Barça right flank. He is repelled once again by this over-worked Villa back line, Suzuki rushing off his line to block a shot from a tight angle.
 “I know I have my beer goggles on but aside from Yamal and giving the ball away at the back, Villa, I think, have created more chances,” emails Richard.
 “I appreciate those two factors could be enough to lose by a large score!”
 Share Updated at  16.10 EST 21m ago 16.06 EST Second half kick off
 Rodri has gone off. Marc Bernal is on for Barça. Boost for Villa?
 Share 23m ago 16.05 EST Crisis club Manchester United are losing 2-0 to Roma at half-time. Gulp.
 Manchester United v Roma: Champions League – live Read more Alas, poor Carrick.
 Share 24m ago 16.03 EST Isn’t the Champions League theme tune a blatant rip-off of Barcelona, the 1987 Freddie Mercury and Monserrat Caballé classic?
 Food for thought.
 “Barcelona” Share 37m ago 15.50 EST Half time: Barcelona 1-0 Aston Villa
 A shockingly poor goal for Villa to concede early doors: and there was another stinking attempt to play it out from the back by Suzuki that they got away with. But other than that, Emery’s side have been good.
 Barcelona have been good, too, but can certainly be “got at”.
 Half time reading:
 Arteta backs Saliba’s readiness to return for Arsenal at Slavia Prague Read more Phil Foden sets sights on England recall and says he has had no contact with Tuchel Read more Andoni Iraola calls on Liverpool to sharpen up in attack before Fenerbahce test Read more Share Updated at  15.52 EST 40m ago 15.48 EST 43 min: Cubarsi and Jackson go for a 50-50 near halfway. Both hit the deck. Cubarsi isn’t happy, and when Jackson goes back to “help” him up, there is a bit of a flare-up, with others coming to get involved in the fun.
 Studs were showing there from Jackson there is a check for a red card … it’s not a horrendous challenge by any means, but this is probably going to be …
 No! Check over. I feared the worst there. It’s a yellow card for Raphinha, for getting involved after, and one for Jackson too for the challenge on Cubarsi.
 Share Updated at  15.48 EST 43m ago 15.44 EST 40 min: “Aside from giving it away on the edge of the box, Villa have done great,” says Gerrard on commentary. Which is a fair point. (I’m paraphrasing him slightly.) They’ve looked good, they’ve tried to play and created chances. But the reckless playing-it-out-from-the-back has to stop.
 Share Updated at  15.45 EST 46m ago 15.42 EST 38 min: Lamine Yamal is good at football. Granted, everyone out there on the pitch is, but he really is a class apart. The problem for Villa is he can create chances for himself and others seemingly effortlessly, and no matter how much pressure Villa apply at the other end, Barcelona have a world-class outlet to take advantage of at their leisure. Right on cue, Lamine Yamal produces a ridiculous nutmeg pass, angled from the right wing, to create yet another decent chance.
 View image in fullscreen Lamine Yamal shows some deft close control as he attempts to best Ian Maatsen and Emiliano Buendia. Photograph: Matthieu Mirville/DPPI/Shutterstock Share Updated at  16.08 EST 48m ago 15.39 EST 36 min: Jackson finds yet more space down the Villa right. He’s one-on-one with Fariñas. Manzambi is screaming for it at the far post … Jackson’s eventual shot is deflected out for a corner. The set-piece drops dangerously in the six-yard box but there is no Villa foot or head there to meet it.
 Share Updated at  15.40 EST 50m ago 15.38 EST 34 min: The vast majority of Barcelona’s attack has gone down the right, mostly through Lamine Yamal. But now it’s Raphinha, who pounces on a loose ball near halfway, and streaks into the Villa area. He nearly fashions an opportunity to shoot but Villa manage to deal with it. Just.
 Share Updated at  15.40 EST 53m ago 15.35 EST 31 min: Manzambi goes close for Villa! Barcelona are being generous at the back, in terms of allowing these Villa forwards space to run at them. Manzambi cuts in and out, creating a chance for himself, and hits a shot straight at García! Good from Villa, good from the Switzerland international.
 Share Updated at  15.36 EST 54m ago 15.34 EST 30 min: López battles hard to win the ball back high for Barcelona , and is then clattered by Buendía. The referee books the Argentinian at the earliest opportunity.
 On the touchline, Emery looks deeply concerned, and you can understand why.
 Share 1h ago 15.31 EST 28 min: Lamine Yamal bends a ludicrous pass inside, behind the Villa back line, looking for Raphinha. Is he offside? It’s academic, because his touch is heavy and he cannot control the ball. Lovely delivery by Lamine Yamal all the same.
 Share 1h ago 15.30 EST 26 min: Oh my. Oh dear! What are Villa doing? What sort of thing is happening here? Suzuki tries to play it out from the back again and it’s obvious, before he even does it, what the upshot is going to be. Sure enough the ball is lost on the edge, and Gordon hammers a shot from an angle, that is saved in desperate fashion by the Villa goalie.
 Share Updated at  15.30 EST 1h ago 15.28 EST 24 min: Lamine Yamal is making short work of Maatsen down the Barcelona right, thus far, it is true.
 My team talk for Villa (like it always in the glory days at five-a-side) would have been: “Just keep it tight at the back early on, lads.” To be fair, that would have been very useful advice.
 View image in fullscreen Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal takes on Ian Maatsen of Aston Villa. Photograph: Pedro Salado/Getty Images Share Updated at  15.59 EST 1h ago 15.26 EST 23 min: “This new iteration of the Villa team has come together faster than I could possibly have imagined,” emails Benjamin. “But our defence could have done with strengthening even before the summer’s team evisceration, and where Cash, Lindelof and Pau are all very good - on their day - this is not a wholly confident Villa fan assuming my stool in the Frog & Fiddle.
 “While Gordon has stepped up magnificently post-move, and is legitimately a part of an intimidating Barça attack, Cash has the chops to match him… Maatsen vs Yamal, though … stuff of nightmares!
 “This will be a fascinating test of this nascent team. Our season doesn’t hinge on this, but a win would probably outstrip the achievements of the prior Champion’s League campaign.”
 Share 1h ago 15.23 EST 20 min: Villa counter down the right, and quickly. Manzambi plays Jackson in, and he’s in acres of space due to Barcelona’s high line: the forward suddenly has just the goalie to beat! But García comes way, way out of his area and puts in a vital tackle.
 Share Updated at  15.24 EST 1h ago 15.22 EST 19 min: Another chance for Villa! Manzambi meets a square ball from Jackson, from the Villa right, but he scuffs it horribly! McGinn did well to step over the ball and leave it for Manzambi there.
 Share 1h ago 15.20 EST 16 min: A dangerous run by Gordon down the hosts’ left. He squares the ball low but neither Raphinha nor Lamine Yamal can meet the cross with an effort on goal.
 They replay the goal on telly: Lamine Yamal was exceptionally alert to the possibility of Joan García playing the horrible pass that he did after the pass out from Suzuki. It was so naive from Villa. And Emery will be disgusted to have conceded such a soft goal. Still, there is still hope …
 Share Updated at  15.20 EST 1h ago 15.17 EST 14 min: McGinn pumps a ball down into the left channel looking for the run of Jackson. Joan García, the goalie, plays sweeper and deals with it easily. Still, Villa don’t look intimidated, even if they’ve handed Barcelona a one-goal lead on a silver platter.
 Share Updated at  15.17 EST 1h ago 15.15 EST 13 min: Lamine Yamal sprints to the byline again with the ball under his command. But then, the ball sneaks out for a goal kick before he squares it.
 Oh, he is human!
 Share 1h ago 15.14 EST 11 min: Maatsen goes in the book after Lamine Yamal mugs him off, touching the ball past the Villa defender, and going to ground. Now a nervy disciplinary tightrope to walk for the full-back for a mere 80min or so …
